questions.question: Under what condition is Newton’s second law applicable?
questions.solution_html:
• Under what condition is Newton’s second law F =ma applicable?
  • Newton's second law in the form F=ma is applicable only when:
  • The mass of the body remains constant during its motion.
  • The motion is observed in an inertial (non-accelerating) frame of reference. (2 marks)

questions.question: Explain the significance of conservation of angular momentum in the case of Earth-Moon system.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the significance of conservation of angular momentum in the case of Earth-
  • Moon system.
  • The Moon’s gravity raises two tidal bulges on Earth, and because Earth
  • rotates faster than the Moon orbits, the bulge nearest the Moon is dragged
  • slightly ahead. This creates a gravitational torque that slows down Earth’s
  • rotation, decreasing its rotational angular momentum. At the same time, this
  • torque transfers angular momentum to the Moon, causing it to move
  • gradually farther away from Earth and increase its orbital angular
  • momentum. Although Earth’s rotation slows, the total angular momentum of
  • the Earth–Moon system remains constant, and over billions of years, this
  • process will continue until Earth’s day becomes equal to the Moon’s orbital
  • period, making one day as long as one month.
  • Conservation
  • of angular
  • momentum
  • only (1 mark)

questions.question: How can angular momentum of a system of particles be split into angular momentum of centre of mass and angular momentum about centre of mass.
questions.solution_html:
• How can angular momentum of a system of particles be split into angular
  • momentum of centre of mass and angular momentum about centre of mass.
  • In a system of particles, the internal torques particles exert on each other do not affect the angular
  • momentum of the system, just as internal forces do not affect linear momentum. Therefore, the total
  • angular momentum can be considered as the angular momentum of the centre of mass and the angular
  • momentum of these particles about the centre of mass.

questions.question: What is a damped harmonic oscillator? Write the equation for damping term. Obtain the differential equation of damped harmonic oscillator.
questions.solution_html:
• What is a damped harmonic oscillator? Write the equation for the damping term. Obtain
  • the differential equation of damped harmonic oscillator.
  • A damped harmonic oscillator is a system that experiences a periodic,
  • oscillating force, but is also subjected to an external, non-conservative force
  • that is proportional to the velocity and opposes the motion. This dissipative
  • force causes the system’s mechanical energy and the amplitude of
  • oscillations to decrease gradually over time until the system eventually
  • comes to rest.
  • The equation for the damping force,
  • 𝐹⃗da௠௣௜ⁿ௚ = −𝑏𝑣⃗ = −𝑏𝑑𝑥𝑑𝑡
  • Where b is the damping coefficient
  • 𝑣⃗ is the velocity of the oscillator
  • The forces acting on a damped oscillator of mass m are:
  • Restoring force 𝐹⃗re௦௧௢r௜ⁿ௚ = −𝑘𝑥 and
